In the spring, second month of the first year of Zhèngshǐ, on the *yǐchǒu* day,

the titles of Privy Councilor and Supervisor of the Central Secretariat Liú Fàng, and Privy Councilor and Director of the Central Secretariat Sūn Zī were augmented to Left and Right Grand Masters of Glorious Happiness.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
due to the people of Wèn and Běifēng counties in Liáodōng having migrated and crossed the sea,
the areas of Xī’ān, Línzī, and Chāngguó counties in Qíjùn commandery were designated as Xīnwèn and Nánfēng counties
to accommodate the displaced people.
From the twelfth month of last winter until this month, there was no rain.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
an edict ordered prison officials to promptly rectify unjust cases and
release those with minor offenses;
all high ministers and gentlemen were to offer honest words and excellent counsel,
each giving their utmost.
In the summer, fourth month,
General of Chariots and Cavalry Huáng Quán passed away.
In the autumn, seventh month,
an edict stated:
“The *Yì Jīng* states: ‘To diminish the superior and augment the inferior,’
regulating with institutions and measures,
neither harming wealth
nor harming the people.
Currently, the common people are in want, yet the imperial treasury extensively produces gold, silver, and various other items.
What purpose will this serve?
Now, one hundred and fifty kinds of gold and silver items,
weighing over eighteen hundred *jīn*, are to be taken out
and melted down to supply military needs.”
In the eighth month,
the imperial carriage inspected the autumn harvest in the Luòyáng area,
and gifts were bestowed upon the elderly and diligent farmers, each according to their merits.
In the spring, second month of the second year,
the Emperor first began to study the *Lúnyǔ*,
and commanded the Grand Master of Ceremonies to offer a grand sacrifice to Confucius at Bìyōng,
with Yán Yuān as his co-sacrificed.
In the summer, fifth month,
the Wú generals Zhū Rán and others besieged Fánchéng in Xiāngyáng.
Grand Tutor Sīmǎ Xuānwáng led his troops to resist them.
On the *xīnchǒu* day of the sixth month,
they retreated.
On the *jǐmǎo* day, Wáng Líng, General Who Attacks the East, was made General of Chariots and Cavalry.
In the winter, twelfth month,
there was an earthquake in Nán’ān Commandery.
Nán’ān Commandery experienced an earthquake.
In the spring, first month of the third year,
Prince Huī of Dōngpíng passed away.
In the third month,
Grand Commandant Mǎn Chǒng passed away.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the *jiǎshēn* day,
there was an earthquake in Nán’ān Commandery.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Jiǎng Jì, General of the Palace Guard, was made Grand Commandant.
In the winter, twelfth month,
there was an earthquake in Wèijùn Commandery.
In the spring, first month of the fourth year,
the Emperor came of age,
and gifts were bestowed upon his ministers, each according to their rank.
In the summer, fourth month, on the *yǐmǎo* day,
Empress Zhēn was established,
and a general amnesty was declared.
On the first day of the fifth month,
there was a solar eclipse,
which was total.
In the autumn, seventh month,

an edict commanded that the former Grand Marshal Cáo Zhēn, Cáo Xiū, General-in-Chief Who Conquers the South Xiàhóu Shàng, Grand Master of Ceremonies Huán Jiē, Minister of Works Chén Qún, Grand Tutor Zhōng Yáo, General of Chariots and Cavalry Zhāng Hé, Left General Xú Huǎng, Former General Zhāng Liáo, Right General Lè Jìn, Grand Commandant Huá Xīn, Minister over the Masses Wáng Lǎng, General of Agile Cavalry Cáo Hóng, General Who Conquers the West Xiàhóu Yuān, Rear General Zhū Líng, Wén Pìn, Bearer of the Golden Mace Zāng Bà, General Who Breaks the Barbarians Lǐ Diǎn, General Who Establishes Righteousness Páng Dé, and Colonel of Martial Might Diǎn Wéi be sacrificed to in the temple courtyard of Grand Ancestor [Cáo Cāo].
In the winter, twelfth month,
Queen Bìmíhū of the Wō kingdom sent envoys to offer tribute.
In the spring, second month of the fifth year,
an edict commanded General-in-Chief Cáo Shuǎng to lead his troops to conquer Shǔ.
In the summer, fourth month, on the first day,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *guǐsì* day of the fifth month,
the *Shàngshū* classic was lectured upon and mastered,
and the Grand Master of Ceremonies was commanded to offer a grand sacrifice to Confucius at Bìyōng,
with Yán Yuān as his co-sacrificed;
gifts were bestowed upon the Grand Tutor, General-in-Chief, and those who lectured, each according to their merits.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day, General-in-Chief Cáo Shuǎng led his army back.
In the autumn, eighth month,
Qín Wáng Xún passed away.
In the ninth month,
the Xiānbēi submitted and joined the empire.
The subordinate state of Liáodōng was established,
and Chānglí County was established to accommodate them.
In the winter, eleventh month, on the *guǐmǎo* day,
an edict commanded that the former Director of the Imperial Secretariat Xún Yōu be sacrificed to in the temple courtyard of Grand Ancestor [Cáo Cāo].
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
the state of Qín was restored as Jīngzhào Commandery.
In the twelfth month,
Minister of Works Cuī Lín passed away.
Cuī Lín, Minister of Works, passed away.
In the sixth year, in spring, the second month, on the *dīngmǎo* day,
an earthquake occurred in Nán’ān Commandery.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Zhào Yǎn (趙儼), General of Agile Cavalry, was appointed Minister of Works (Sīkōng).
In summer, the sixth month,
Yǎn (儼) passed away.
In the eighth month, on the *dīngmǎo* day,
Gāo Ròu (高柔), Grand Astrologer (Tàicháng), was appointed Minister of Works (Sīkōng).
On the *guǐsì* day,
Liú Fàng (劉放), Grand Master of Glorious Happiness of the Left (Zuǒ Guānglù Dàfū), was appointed General of Agile Cavalry (Piàojì Jiāngjūn),
and Sūn Zī (孫資), Grand Master of Glorious Happiness of the Right (Yòu Guānglù Dàfū), was appointed General of the Guards (Wèijiāngjūn).
In winter, the eleventh month,
the ancestral temple of Tàizǔ (太祖) was ritually honored (xiápjì).
For the first time, the twenty-one meritorious ministers who aided in the founding of the dynasty, as previously discussed, were sacrificed to.
In the twelfth month, on the *xīnhài* day,
an edict was issued that the Commentary on the *Yì* (Yìzhuàn) written by the late Minister over the Masses (Sītú) Wáng Lǎng (王朗)
should be used by scholars for examination and testing.
On the *yǐhài* day,
an edict stated:
“Tomorrow, there will be a grand assembly of all officials.
Order the Grand Mentor (Tàifù) to ascend the hall in the imperial carriage.”
In the seventh year, in spring, the second month,
Wúqiū Jiǎn (毋丘儉), Inspector (Cìshǐ) of Yōuzhōu, launched a campaign against Gāogōulí,
and in summer, the fifth month,
he campaigned against Huì Mò (濊貊).
He defeated them all.
Hán Nàxī (韓那奚) and dozens of other states each led their tribes to surrender.
In autumn, the eighth month, on the *wùshēn* day,
an edict stated:
“Recently, I saw in the market some government slaves and bondmaids being sold,
all of whom were seventy years old,
or afflicted with chronic illness and disability,
these are the so-called impoverished of the celestial people.
Moreover, the government sells them again after their strength is exhausted,
which is indefensible both in terms of advance and retreat.
Let them all be released as common people.
If there are any who cannot support themselves,
the commanderies and counties shall provide relief to them.”
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
an edict stated:
“I am to personally offer sacrifices on the nineteenth day,
but yesterday, when I went out, I saw that the roads were already being repaired.
If it rains, they will have to be repaired again,
which is a futile waste of effort.
I constantly think of the common people, who have little strength but many labor duties,
and I keep them in my heart day and night.
Roads should only be required to be open and convenient.
I hear that the old and young are being beaten,
striving to make elaborate repairs,
causing them to be exhausted and wander,
even leading to lamentation.
How can I feel at ease riding on such roads
and thereby bringing honor to the ancestral temple?
From now on,
clearly reiterate this order.”
In winter, the twelfth month,
the *Lǐjì* (Lǐjì) was thoroughly studied.
The Grand Astrologer (Tàicháng) was ordered to offer a Grand Sacrifice (Tàiláo) to Kǒngzǐ (孔子) at the Bìyōng,
with Yán Yuān (顏淵) as his co-sacrificial recipient.
In the eighth year, in spring, the second month, on the first day,
there was a solar eclipse.
In summer, the fifth month,
the ten counties north of the Fén River (Fénběi) in Hédōng Commandery were separated to form Píngyáng Commandery.
In autumn, the seventh month,
Hé Yàn (何晏), Palace Assistant Imperial Clerk (Shàngshū), presented a memorial, stating:
“One who is good at governing a state must first govern oneself.
One who governs oneself must be careful about what one learns.
If what one learns is correct, then one’s person is correct;
if one’s person is correct, then one acts without being commanded.
If what one learns is not correct, then one’s person is not correct;
if one’s person is not correct, then one will not obey even when commanded.
Therefore, as a ruler,
one must choose righteous people to associate with,
and observe righteous examples.
One should banish the sounds of Zhèng (Zhèngshēng) and not listen to them,
and keep sycophants at a distance and not draw near to them.
Only then will evil thoughts not arise and the righteous path can be extended.
In the late period, ignorant rulers,
not knowing how to gain or lose,
expelled gentlemen,
and drew near to petty individuals.
Loyal and good people were estranged,
while flatterers were intimate and familiar.
Disorder arises from close intimacy,
like the rats in the temple and shrines.
Examining their wisdom or foolishness,
this is what they have accumulated,
hence the constant and earnest exhortations of the sages.
Shùn (舜) admonished Yǔ (禹), saying ‘Beware of your neighbors! Beware of your neighbors!’,
meaning be careful of those close to you.
Zhōu Gōng (周公) admonished King Chéng (成王), saying ‘Beware of your companions! Beware of your companions!’,
meaning be careful of those you associate with.
The [Shū] states: ‘If one person has blessings,
the myriad people will rely on him.’
From now on,
when Your Majesty visits the Shìgān Hall (Shìgān Diàn) or roams in the imperial garden,
let all high officials attend.
During relaxed gatherings and feasts,
they can also review documents,
consult on government affairs,
and discuss the meaning of the classics,
serving as a model for ten thousand generations.”
In winter, the twelfth month,
Kǒng Yì (孔乂), Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary (Sànqí Chángshì) and Remonstrance Official (Jiàn Yì Dàfū), presented a memorial, stating:
“According to the Rites,
the palaces of the Son of Heaven
have regulations regarding carving and polishing,
but no decorations of vermilion or red.
It is fitting to follow the Rites and restore ancient practices.
Now the empire is peaceful,
and the distinction between ruler and minister is clear.
Your Majesty should simply not slacken in your position,
maintain a fair and just heart,
and administer rewards and punishments carefully to command them.
You should cease riding horses in the imperial garden.
When you go out, you must always use a palanquin or carriage.
This would be a blessing for the empire,
and the wish of your ministers and subjects.”
Both Yàn (晏) and Yì (乂) took the opportunity of imperial leisure to offer admonitions.
In the ninth year, in spring, the second month,
Sūn Zī (孫資), General of the Guards (Wèijiāngjūn) and Prefect of the Central Secretariat (Zhōngshū Lìng),
on the *guǐsì* day,
Liú Fàng (劉放), General of Agile Cavalry (Piàojì Jiāngjūn) and Director of the Central Secretariat (Zhōngshū Jiān),
and in the third month, on the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Wèi Zhēn (衞臻), Minister over the Masses (Sītú),
each resigned from their posts.
They were granted peerages and returned to their residences,
with the rank of Special Advanced Official (Tèjìn).
In the fourth month,
Gāo Ròu (高柔), Minister of Works (Sīkōng), was appointed Minister over the Masses (Sītú);
Xú Mò (徐邈), Grand Master of Glorious Happiness (Guānglù Dàfū), was appointed Minister of Works (Sīkōng),
but he firmly declined to accept.
In autumn, the ninth month,
Wáng Líng (王淩), General of Chariots and Cavalry (Chējì Jiāngjūn), was appointed Minister of Works (Sīkōng).
In winter, the tenth month,
a great wind tore off roofs and broke trees.
In the first year of Jiāpíng (嘉平), in spring, the first month, on the *jiǎwǔ* day,
the imperial carriage visited Gāopíng Tomb (Gāopíng Líng).

Sīmǎ Xuānwáng (司馬宣王), Grand Mentor (Tàifù), memorialized for the removal of the titles of Grand General (Dàjiāngjūn) Cáo Shuǎng (曹爽), his younger brother Xī (羲), Central Imperial Clerk (Zhōnglǐngjūn), Wǔwèi General (Wǔwèi Jiāngjūn) Xùn (訓), and Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary (Sànqí Chángshì) Yàn (彥).
They were granted peerages and returned to their residences.
On the *wùxū* day,
the relevant officials memorialized to arrest Huángmén (黃門) Zhāng Dāng (張當) and hand him over to the Grand Judge (Tíngwèi).
After interrogation and confirmation of his testimony,
it was revealed that Shuǎng (爽) had conspired in rebellion.

Furthermore, Palace Assistant Imperial Clerk (Shàngshū) Dīng Mì (丁謐), Dèng Yáng (鄧颺), Hé Yàn (何晏), Inspector of the Capital Region (Sīlì Xiàowèi) Bì Guǐ (畢軌), Inspector (Cìshǐ) of Jīngzhōu Lǐ Shèng (李勝), and Grand Minister of Agriculture (Dàsīnóng) Huán Fàn (桓範) had all conspired with Shuǎng (爽).
Their three familial clans were exterminated.
The details are in the biography of Shuǎng (爽).
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
a general amnesty was proclaimed.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
Sīmǎ Xuānwáng (司馬宣王), Grand Mentor (Tàifù), was appointed Chancellor (Chéngxiàng),
but he firmly declined, and so the appointment ceased.
In summer, the fourth month, on the *yǐchǒu* day,
the reign year was changed.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Jiǎng Jì (蔣濟), Grand Commandant (Tàiwèi), passed away.
In winter, the twelfth month, on the *xīnmǎo* day,
Wáng Líng (王淩), Minister of Works (Sīkōng), was appointed Grand Commandant (Tàiwèi).
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Sūn Lǐ (孫禮), Inspector of the Capital Region (Sīlì Xiàowèi), was appointed Minister of Works (Sīkōng).
In the second year, in summer, the fifth month,
Guō Huái (郭淮), General Who Conquers the West (Zhēngxī Jiāngjūn), was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry (Chējì Jiāngjūn).
In winter, the tenth month,
Sūn Zī (孫資), Special Advanced Official (Tèjìn), was appointed General of Agile Cavalry (Piàojì Jiāngjūn).
In the eleventh month,
Sūn Lǐ (孫禮), Minister of Works (Sīkōng), passed away.
In the twelfth month, on the *jiǎchén* day,
Lín (霖), Prince of Dōnghǎi (Dōnghǎi Wáng), passed away.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Wáng Chǎng (王昶), General Who Conquers the South (Zhēngnán Jiāngjūn), crossed the Yangtze River (Jiāng),
and launched a surprise attack on Wú (吳),
defeating it.
In the spring, the first month of the third year,
Wáng Jī, Inspector of Jīngzhōu, and Chén TàI, Administrator of Xīnchéng Commandery, attacked Wú,
and defeated them.
Several thousand surrendered.
In the second month,
Yílíng County of Nánjùn was established to house the surrendered and attached.
In the third month,
Sīmǎ Fú, Minister of the Imperial Secretariat, was made Grand Minister of Works.
In the fourth month, on the day jiǎshēn,
Wáng Chǎng, General who Conquers the South, was made Grand General who Conquers the South.
On the day rénchén,
a general amnesty was issued.
On the day bǐngwǔ,
it was heard that Wáng Líng, Grand Commandant, planned to depose the emperor
and install Prince Biao of Chǔ.
Sīmǎ Xuān Wáng, Grand Tutor, marched east to subdue Líng.
In the fifth month, on the day jiǎyín,
Líng committed suicide.
In the sixth month,
Biao was granted death.
In the autumn, the seventh month, on the day rénxū,
Empress Zhēn passed away.
On the day xīnwèi,
Sīmǎ Fú, Grand Minister of Works, was made Grand Commandant.
On the day wùyín,
Sīmǎ Xuān Wáng, Grand Tutor, passed away.
Sīmǎ Jǐng Wáng, General of the Guards, was made General of the Guarding Army,
and recorded the affairs of the Imperial Secretariat.
On the day yǐwèi,
Empress Huái Zhēn was interred at Tàiqīng Mausoleum.
On the day gēngzǐ,
Sūn Zī, General of Agile Cavalry, passed away.
In the eleventh month,
the relevant authorities memorialized that among the meritorious officials who should receive sacrifices at the temple of Tàizǔ,
their ranks should be reordered by their official positions,
and Sīmǎ Xuān Wáng, Grand Tutor, whose achievements were great and rank honorable,
should be placed at the very top.
In the twelfth month,
Zhèng Chōng, Court Grandee of Splendid Happiness, was made Grand Minister of Works.
In the spring, the first month, on the day guǐmǎo of the fourth year,
Sīmǎ Jǐng Wáng, General of the Guarding Army, was made Grand General.
In the second month,
Empress Zhāng was enthroned,
and a general amnesty was issued.
In the summer, the fifth month,
two fish
appeared on the roof of the military arsenal.
In the winter, the eleventh month,
an edict ordered Wáng Chǎng, Grand General who Conquers the South, Hú Zūn, General who Attacks the East, Wúqiū Jiǎn, General who Guards the South, and others to attack Wú.
In the twelfth month,
Zhūgě Kè, Grand General of Wú, resisted the attack
and inflicted a great defeat on the armies at Dōngguān.
They returned in disadvantage.
In the summer, the fourth month of the fifth year,
a general amnesty was issued.
In the fifth month,
Zhūgě Kè, Grand Tutor of Wú, besieged Xīnchéng in Héféi.
An edict ordered Sīmǎ Fú, Grand Commandant, to resist him.
In the autumn, the seventh month,
Kè retreated and returned.
In the eighth month,
an edict stated:
“Guō Xiū, former Imperial Household Grandee of Xīpíng,
honed his integrity and refined his conduct,
maintaining an unwavering heart.
Recently, Jiāng Wéi, a general of Shǔ, plundered Xiū’s commandery
and he was captured.
Last year, Fèi Yī, the false Grand General, led a multitude,
secretly plotting to spy and reconnoiter.
When passing through Hànshòu,
he invited many guests to a gathering.
Xiū, in the midst of the large assembly, personally slew Yī with a blade.
His courage surpassed that of Niè Zhèng,
and his achievement exceeded that of Jiè Zǐ.
He can be said to have sacrificed his life for benevolence
and abandoned life for righteousness.
To posthumously commend and honor him
is to display and extol loyalty and righteousness;
to bestow blessings upon his descendants
is to encourage future generations.
Therefore, Xiū is posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Chánglè Township,
with a thousand households as his revenue fief,
and granted the posthumous title Wēi Hóu.
His son shall inherit the title,
and additionally be appointed Attendant Officer of Carriages.
A thousand ingots of silver and
a thousand bolts of silk shall be bestowed
to glorify the honored, both living and deceased,
and to forever inspire future generations.”
From the emperor’s ascension to the throne until this year,
many commanderies, states, counties, and districts were established or abolished,
and then sometimes restored.
They are too numerous to record.
In the spring, the second month, on the day jǐchǒu of the sixth year,
Wúqiū Jiǎn, General who Suppresses the East, memorialized:
“Previously, when Zhūgě Kè besieged Xīnchéng in Héféi,
the city dispatched a soldier, Liú Zhěng, to break through the siege and transmit intelligence.
He was captured by the enemy.
When interrogated about his mission,
they said to Zhěng: ‘Grandee Zhūgě wishes to spare your life,
so you may confess fully.’
Zhěng cursed, saying: ‘You dead dogs,
what kind of talk is this!
I am bound to die and become a ghost for the state of Wèi.
I will not meekly seek to live,
nor will I follow you.
If you wish to kill me,
then kill me quickly.’
He offered no other words.
Another soldier, Zhèng Xiàng, was dispatched from the city to transmit intelligence.
Someone reported this to Kè,
who sent cavalry to search along the siege line
and captured Xiàng.
Four or five men bound his head and face,
and led him around the outside of the city.
They ordered Xiàng
to shout loudly,
saying, ‘The main army has already returned to Luò,
so you might as well surrender early.’
Xiàng did not follow their words.
Instead, he shouted loudly to those in the city: ‘The main army is close, just outside the siege!
Brave men, exert yourselves!’
The bandits used a knife to prod his mouth
to prevent him from speaking,
but Xiàng continued to shout loudly,
making sure those in the city heard and knew.
Zhěng and Xiàng, as soldiers,
were able to uphold righteousness and maintain integrity.
Their children and younger brothers should receive special distinction.”
An edict stated:
“High titles are given to commend great achievements,
and generous rewards are bestowed to honor valiant warriors.
Zhěng and Xiàng, in volunteering for a mission to convey messages,
braved heavy sieges,
rushed through naked blades,
lightly regarded their lives to uphold their trust.
Though unfortunately captured,
their integrity remained steadfast.
They proclaimed the great might of the six armies,
and calmed the fearful hearts of the city defenders.
Facing danger, they did not waver,
and completed their mission to deliver the message.
In the past, Xiè Yáng, when captured by Chǔ,
preferred death to disloyalty.
The Grand Master of the Middle Road of Qí accomplished his mission through death.
Compared to Zhěng and Xiàng,
none could surpass them.
Now, Zhěng and Xiàng are posthumously granted the title Marquis within the Pass,
each having their soldier status removed,
and their sons shall inherit the title,
following the precedent for a section commander who dies in service.”
On the day gēngxū,
Lǐ Fēng, Minister of the Central Secretariat, and Zhāng Jī, Court Grandee of Splendid Happiness and father of the Empress, conspired to depose and replace high officials,
making Xiàhóu Xuán, Grand Master of Sacrificial Worship, the Grand General.
The plot was discovered,
and all those implicated were executed.
On the day xīnhài,
a general amnesty was issued.
In the third month,
Empress Zhāng was deposed.
In the summer, the fourth month,
Empress Wáng was enthroned,
and a general amnesty was issued.
In the fifth month,
Wáng Kuí, Attendant Officer of Carriages and father of the Empress, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Guǎngmíng Township and Court Grandee of Splendid Happiness,
holding the rank of Special Advanced.
His wife, Lady Tián, was made Lady of Xuānyáng Township.
In the autumn, the ninth month,
Sīmǎ Jǐng Wáng, Grand General, planned to depose the emperor
and reported it to the Empress Dowager.
On the day jiǎxū,
the Empress Dowager issued an order, stating:
“Emperor Fāng has already reached maturity,
but does not personally attend to all affairs of state.
He indulges in internal pleasures,
is immersed in female virtue,
daily invites entertainers and actors,
and allows their ugly jests.
He welcomes the families of the Six Palaces to stay in the inner chambers,
destroying human relationships,
and disrupting the distinctions between men and women.
His reverence and filial piety diminish daily,
and his perversity grows exceedingly.
He cannot inherit the celestial lineage
or offer sacrifices to the ancestral temples.
Let Gāo Ròu, who also holds the office of Grand Commandant, present the credentials,
and make a great martial announcement to the ancestral temples.
Fāng shall be sent back to his fief as Prince of Qí,
to abdicate the imperial throne.”
On that day, he moved to a separate palace,
at the age of twenty-three.
Envoys, bearing credentials, escorted him,
and constructed the palace for the Prince of Qí in Zhòngmén of Hénèi,
with all regulations adhering to the rites of a princely state.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
an edict stated:
“Lín, the Prince of Dōnghǎi,
is the son of Gāozǔ Wén Huángdì.
Lín’s sons
are intimately related to the state.
Máo, the Duke of Gāoguì Xiāng, possesses the capacity for great accomplishments;
he shall be made the successor to Míng Huángdì.”
The Duke of Gāoguì Xiāng’s personal name was Máo,
his courtesy name was Yànshì.
He was the grandson of Wén Dì
and the son of Lín, the Prince Dì of Dōnghǎi.
In the fifth year of Zhèngshǐ,
he was enfeoffed as the Duke of Gāoguì Xiāng of Tán Xiàn.
He was fond of learning in his youth
and matured early.
When the Prince of Qí was deposed,
the high officials debated inviting and establishing the Duke.
On the *jǐchǒu* day of the tenth month,
the Duke arrived at Xuánwǔ Guǎn.
The assembled officials requested that he reside in the front hall,
but the Duke, considering it the former residence of the deceased emperor,
avoided it and stayed in the west wing.
The assembled officials again requested to welcome him with a full imperial procession,
but the Duke refused.
On the *gēngyín* day,
the Duke entered Luòyáng.
The assembled officials welcomed and bowed to him south of the Xīyèmén gate.
The Duke alighted from his carriage, about to return the bow,
when the usher requested:
“Protocol dictates no bowing.”
The Duke said:
“I am a subject.”
He then returned the bow.
He alighted from his carriage at Zhǐchēmén.
His attendants said:
“It was customary for the imperial carriage to enter.”
The Duke said:
“I have been summoned by the Empress Dowager,
and I do not yet know what is to be done!”
He then walked to Tàijí Dōngtáng
and was presented to the Empress Dowager.
On that very day, he ascended the imperial throne in Tàijí Qiándiàn.
The hundreds of officials present were overjoyed.
An imperial edict stated:
“In the past, the Three Ancestors, with their divine martiality and sagely virtue,
responded to Heaven and received the mandate.
The Prince of Qí, upon succeeding to the throne,
acted without restraint and beyond measure,
overthrowing his virtue.
The Empress Dowager, deeply contemplating the grave importance of the altars of soil and grain,
accepted the counsel of the chief ministers,
and thus replaced his position,
gathering the great mandate to Me alone.
With My insignificant person,
entrusted above the princes and dukes,
day and night I am reverent and fearful,
fearing that I cannot continue and uphold the great teachings of My ancestors,
and restore the grand enterprise of restoration.
I am utterly vigilant and cautious,
as if on the brink of a chasm.
Now, the dukes and high officials, My trusted aides,
and the assistants from all four directions, who exert their strength in campaigns and garrisons,
have all accumulated virtue and achieved merit,
loyally and diligently serving the imperial house.
May I rely on the virtuous ministers of My ancestors and late father
to assist this young man,
so as to protect and govern the imperial house,
allowing Me, despite My ignorance,
to rule with folded hands.
It is said that the way of a ruler
is to have virtue as profound as Heaven and Earth,
and benevolence spread across the four seas.
He should lead with compassion and love,
and demonstrate his likes and dislikes,
only then will education and transformation prevail from above,
and the common people obey from below.
Although I am without virtue
and ignorant of the Great Way,
I wish to reach this path together with all within the realm.
Does not the *Shū* say: ‘He who brings peace to the people will be benevolent,
and the common people will cherish him.’ ”
There was a general amnesty,
and the reign era was changed.
Expenditures for imperial carriages, attire, and the needs of the imperial harem were reduced,
and useless extravagant and elaborate items produced by the various artisans of the Shàngfāng Imperial Office were abolished.
In the first year of Zhèngyuán, in the winter, on the *rénchén* day of the tenth month,
Chamberslains were dispatched with credentials to the four directions,
to observe customs,
comfort soldiers and common people,
and investigate those who were wronged or had lost their positions.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Grand General Sīmǎ Jǐng Wáng was granted the yellow *yuè* axe,
the privilege of not hastening in court,
not being addressed by name when presenting memorials,
and wearing swords and shoes while ascending the hall.
On the *wùxū* day,
a yellow dragon was seen in a well in Yè.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
officials were ordered to discuss the merits of deposing and establishing, and setting strategy,
and titles, increased fiefs, promotions, and graded rewards were distributed accordingly.
In the second year, in the spring, on the *yǐchǒu* day of the first month,
Zhèn Dōng Jiāngjūn Qiū Jiǎn and Yángzhōu Cìshǐ Wén Qīn rebelled.
(On the *wùxū* day) [On the *wùyín* day],
Grand General Sīmǎ Jǐng Wáng marched against them.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
Chēqí Jiāngjūn Guō Huái died.
In the intercalary month, on the *jǐhài* day,
Qīn was defeated at Yuèjiā.
Qīn fled,
and consequently defected to Wú.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
(the Dūwèi of Ānfēng Huáijīn) [the Dūwèi of Ānfēng Jīn] beheaded Jiǎn,
and sent his head to the capital.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
a special amnesty was again granted to the soldiers and common people of Huáinán who had been misled by Jiǎn and Qīn.
Zhūgě Dàn, the Zhèn Nán Jiāngjūn, was appointed Zhèn Dōng Dàjiāngjūn.
Sīmǎ Jǐng Wáng died in Xǔchāng.
In the second month, on the *dīngsì* day,
Wèi Jiāngjūn Sīmǎ Wén Wáng was appointed Grand General,
and given authority over the Lu Shangshu Shi.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Wú Grand General Sūn Jùn and others, with a force of ten myriad, arrived at Shòuchūn.
Zhūgě Dàn repelled and defeated them,
beheading Wú Zuǒ Jiāngjūn Liú Zàn,
and presenting the spoils of victory to the capital.
In the third month,
Empress Biàn was established,
and a general amnesty was granted.
In the summer, in the fourth month, on the *jiǎyín* day,
the Empress’s father, Biàn Lóng, was enfeoffed as a Marquis.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
Zhēng Nán Dàjiāngjūn Wáng Chǎng was appointed Piàojí Jiāngjūn.
In the autumn, in the seventh month,
Zhēng Dōng Dàjiāngjūn Hú Zūn was appointed Wèi Jiāngjūn,
and Zhèn Dōng Dàjiāngjūn Zhūgě Dàn was appointed Zhēng Dōng Dàjiāngjūn.
In the eighth month, on the *xīnhài* day,
Shǔ Grand General Jiāng Wéi raided Dí Dào.
Yōngzhōu Cìshǐ Wáng Jīng fought him at Táoxī.
Jīng suffered a great defeat
and returned to defend Dí Dào City.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Chángshuǐ Xiàowèi Dèng Ài was appointed acting Ānxī Jiāngjūn,
to join forces with Zhēng Xī Jiāngjūn Chén Tài to resist Wéi.
On the *wùchén* day,
Tàiwèi Sīmǎ Fú was again dispatched as a reinforcement.
In the ninth month, on the *gēngzǐ* day,
the study of the *Shàngshū* was concluded.
Those who personally received instruction, such as Sīkōng Zhèng Chōng and Shìzhōng Zhèng Xiǎotóng, were given various rewards.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Jiāng Wéi retreated.
In the winter, in the tenth month,
an edict stated:
“I, with My meager virtue,
could not check the aggression of the bandits,
and thus allowed the Shǔ bandits to rampage on the border.
In the battle of Táoxī,
a defeat was suffered,
with officers and soldiers dying,
counted in the thousands.
Some lost their lives on the battlefield,
their wronged souls unreturned;
others were captured by the enemy’s hands,
wandering in foreign lands.
I deeply mourn and pity them,
and My heart grieves for them.
Therefore, order the local commanderies’ Dǐnnóng and the two Hùjūn for pacifying barbarians, along with their chief officials, to console and assist their households,
exempting them from levies and corvée for one year.
As for those who died bravely in battle,
all shall be treated according to the old regulations,
with no omissions.”
In the eleventh month, on the *jiǎwǔ* day,
due to the four commanderies of Lǒngyòu and Jīnchéng
suffering enemy attacks for consecutive years,
and some having defected to the enemy,
their relatives remaining in their homeland were uneasy.
All were granted a special amnesty.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
an edict stated:
“In the past battle of Táoxī,
officers, civil servants, soldiers, and common people either died in battle on the front lines
or drowned in the Táoshuǐ.
Their bones were not collected,
abandoned in the wilderness.
I have always grieved for this.
Therefore, instruct the Zhēngxī and Ānxī Jiāngjūn
to each order their subordinates to search for and retrieve bodies at the battle sites and by the water,
to collect and bury them,
to comfort both the living and the dead.”
In the first year of Gānlù, in the spring, on the *xīnchǒu* day of the first month,
a green dragon was seen in a well in Zhǐ Xiàn.
On the *yǐsì* day,
Pèi Wáng Lín died.
In the summer, in the fourth month, on the *gēngxū* day,
Grand General Sīmǎ Wén Wáng was bestowed the *yǎnmiǎn* ceremonial robes,
with red slippers as accessories.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
the Emperor visited the Imperial Academy,
and asked the various scholars:
"The Sages profoundly supported the divine and intelligent,
looking up and observing down,
and first created the eight trigrams.
Later Sages 重 (doubled) them to sixty-four,
and established the *yáo* lines to exhaust their numbers.
All these great principles
were fully prepared,
yet the Xià (Dynasty) had the *Liánshān*,
the Yīn (Dynasty) had the *Guīcáng*,
and the Zhōu (Dynasty) called it the *Zhōuyì*.
What is the reason
for these names for the book of *Yì*?"
*Yì* Doctor Chúnyú Jùn replied:
"Bāoxī based it on Suìhuáng's diagrams to create the eight trigrams.
Shénnóng expanded them to sixty-four.
Huángdì, Yáo, and Shùn understood their changes.
The Three Dynasties adapted to the times,
with simplicity and refinement each following its own course.
Therefore, *Yì*
means 'change and transformation.'
It was named *Liánshān*,
likening it to mountains producing internal [clouds and] mists,
connecting heaven and earth.
*Guīcáng*
means that all matters are returned and stored within it."
The Emperor then said:
"If Bāoxī indeed based his work on Suìhuáng to create the *Yì*,
why did Kǒngzǐ not say 'when Suìrénshì passed away, Bāoxīshì arose'?"
Jùn could not answer.
The Emperor then asked:
"Kǒngzǐ wrote the *Tuàn* and *Xiàng*,
and Zhèng Xuán wrote annotations.
Although the Sages and worthies differed,
their interpretations of the classic's meaning were one.
Now, the *Tuàn* and *Xiàng* are not connected to the classic text,
but the annotations connect them.
Why is this?"
Jùn replied:
"Zhèng Xuán combined the *Tuàn* and *Xiàng* with the classic
to make it easier for scholars to examine and understand."
The Emperor said:
"If Zhèng Xuán combined them,
it would indeed be convenient for learning.
Then why did Kǒngzǐ not combine them to clarify for scholars?"
Jùn replied:
"Kǒngzǐ feared they might be confused with Wénwáng's text,
and therefore did not combine them.
This was the Sage showing humility by not combining them."
The Emperor said:
"If the Sage showed humility by not combining them,
then why was Zhèng Xuán uniquely not humble?"
Jùn replied:
"Ancient meanings are profound,
and the Sage's questions are recondite and far-reaching.
It is not something your servant can explain in full."
The Emperor then asked:
"The *Xìcí* says 'Huángdì, Yáo, and Shùn let their robes hang down and the world was well-governed.'
This implies that in the eras of Bāoxī and Shénnóng, there were no robes.
But when Sages transform the world,
why such a difference?"
Jùn replied:
"During the time of the Three Sovereigns,
people were few and wild animals were numerous.
Therefore, they took feathers and skins, and the world had enough to use.
When it came to Huángdì,
people were numerous and wild animals were few,
so clothing was made to adapt to the changes of the time."
The Emperor then asked:
"*Qián* represents heaven,
but it also represents metal,
jade,
and old horses.
Are these comparable to insignificant things?"
Jùn replied:
"When the Sage takes images,
some are far, some are near.
Near ones are taken from objects;
far ones are heaven and earth."
After the lecture on the *Yì* was concluded,
the Emperor commanded a lecture on the *Shàngshū*.
The Emperor asked:
"Zhèng Xuán said, 'To examine antiquity and be like Heaven, means Yáo was like Heaven.'
Wáng Sù said, 'Yáo followed the ancient path and acted accordingly.'
These two meanings differ.
Which one is correct?"
*Shàngshū* Doctor Yú Jùn replied:
"The previous scholars' interpretations
each have their discrepancies.
Your servant is not sufficient to settle them.
However, the *Hóngfàn* states: 'When three men divine,
follow the words of two.'
Jiǎ, Mǎ, and Sù all held the view of 'following the ancient path.'
Judging by the *Hóngfàn*,
Sù's meaning is superior."
The Emperor said:
"Zhòngní said, 'Only Heaven is great,
only Yáo patterned himself after it.'
Yáo's great virtue
lay in patterning himself after Heaven.
Following the ancient path
is not its ultimate expression.
Now, the opening passage sets forth the meaning to illustrate Sage-virtue,
and yet abandons its greatness,
instead mentioning its minor points.
Is this the author's intention?"
Jùn replied:
"Your servant adheres to and follows his teacher's explanations,
not yet having comprehended the great meaning.
As for striking a balance,
please decide it with your Sage-like wisdom."
Next, regarding the Four Peaks recommending Gǔn,
the Emperor again asked:
"A great man
matches his virtue with Heaven and Earth,
and his brilliance with the sun and moon.
His thoughts are all-encompassing,
and his clarity illuminates everything.
Now, Wáng Sù says, 'Yáo could not fully understand Gǔn,
and therefore tried him out.'
If this is the case,
does the Sage's clarity have something incomplete?"
Jùn replied:
"Even the Sage, though expansive,
still has something incomplete.
Therefore Yǔ said, 'To know men is to be discerning,
but even the Emperor found it difficult.'
However, he was ultimately able to change and entrust to Sages and worthies,
and brightly cultivate all achievements,
which is also how he became a Sage."
The Emperor said:
"To have a beginning and an end,
this belongs only to the Sage.
If one cannot begin,
how can one be a Sage?
The statement 'even the Emperor found it difficult,'
yet was ultimately able to change the entrustment,
probably means that knowing men
is difficult even for a Sage,
not that he was incomplete.
The classic says: 'To know men is to be discerning,
and to be able to appoint officials.'
If Yáo doubted Gǔn,
and tried him for nine years,
and failed in appointing the official,
how can he be called a discerning Sage?"
Jùn replied:
"Your servant secretly observes from the classics and commentaries
that Sages' actions are not without fault.
Thus, Yáo erred concerning the Four Felons,
Zhōugōng erred concerning the Two Uncles,
and Zhòngní erred concerning Zǎiyǔ."
The Emperor said:
"Yáo's appointment of Gǔn
yielded no results for nine years;
he disrupted the Five Elements,
and the people sank into distress.
As for Zhòngní erring concerning Zǎiyǔ,
the seriousness of the words and actions
is different.
As for the matters of Zhōugōng, Guǎn, and Cài,
which are also recorded in the *Shàngshū*,
these are all things that the doctor should understand."
Jùn replied:
"These are all points of doubt for previous worthies;
they are not something your servant, with his limited insights, can fully investigate."
Next, regarding
"There was a [hidden] *chóng* (multitude/mass) below, named Yú Shùn,"
the Emperor asked:
"During Yáo's time,
floods caused harm,
and the Four Felons were in court.
It was a time to swiftly promote worthy Sages to save the people.
Shùn was already of established age,
and his Sage-virtue was shining,
yet he was not advanced for a long time.
Why was this?"
Jùn replied:
"Yáo sighed and sought worthies,
wishing to cede his position.
The Four Peaks said, 'His virtue is deficient, unfitting for the imperial throne.'
Yáo again instructed the Peaks to recommend obscure individuals,
and only then was Shùn recommended.
The origin of Shùn's recommendation
actually came from Yáo.
This was probably the Sage wanting to exhaust the hearts of the multitude."
The Emperor said:
"Since Yáo already heard of Shùn but did not promote him,
and at that time loyal ministers also did not advance him,
but instead had the Peaks recommend obscure individuals and only then propose him,
this does not show urgency in using a Sage to relieve the people."
Jùn replied:
"This is beyond your servant's foolish understanding to comprehend."
Thereupon, he again ordered the lecture on the Lǐjì (Book of Rites).
The Emperor asked:
“‘The highest virtue is to establish virtue;
the next is to exert oneself in bestowing and repaying.’
How is it that the methods of governance and education differ;
what policies are cultivated to achieve the establishment of virtue,
bestowing without expecting recompense?”
Dóctor Mǎ Zhào replied:
“To establish virtue at the highest level
refers to the eras of the Sān Huáng (Three Sovereigns) and Wǔ Dì (Five Emperors), who transformed the people with virtue.
The next, repaying bestowals,
refers to the eras of the Sān Wáng (Three Kings), who governed with ritual.”
The Emperor said:
“If the effects of transformation in these two are different in depth,
does it mean the rulers had superior or inferior qualities?
Or was it due to the times?”
Zhào replied:
“It is indeed due to the times having simplicity and refinement,
thus the transformation had varying depths.”
In the fifth month,
Yè and Shàngluò both reported that sweet dew had fallen.
In the summer, sixth month, on the bǐngwǔ day,
the era name was changed to Gānlù.
On the yǐchǒu day,
a green dragon was seen in a well in Yuánchéng county.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the jǐmǎo day,
General of the Guards Hú Zūn passed away.
On the guǐwèi day,
General Who Guards the West Dèng Ài greatly defeated the Shǔ great general Jiāng Wéi at Shàngguī.
An edict said:
“The army has not yet exerted its full might,
yet the vile enemy is crushed and broken,
with tens of thousands of heads taken and captives seized.
Since recent victories,
none compare to this.
Now envoys are dispatched to reward and bestow gifts upon the officers and soldiers,
and a grand feast will be held,
with drinking and revelry all day,
to manifest Our intention.”
In the eighth month, on the gēngwǔ day,
Great General Sīmǎ Wén Wáng was ordered to be given the additional title of Grand Commander (Dà Dūdū),
to report matters without being addressed by name,
and to be granted the yellow battle-axe (jiǎ huángyuè).
On the guǐyǒu day,
Grand Commandant (Tàiwèi) Sīmǎ Fú was made Grand Tutor (Tàifù).
In the ninth month,
Minister of Works (Sītú) Gāo Ròu was made Grand Commandant (Tàiwèi).
In the winter, tenth month,
Minister of Education (Sīkōng) Zhèng Chōng was made Minister of Works (Sītú),
and Left Assistant of the Department of State Affairs (Shàngshū Zuǒ Púyè) Lú Yù was made Minister of Education (Sīkōng).
In the second year, spring, second month,
a green dragon was seen in a well in Wēn county.
In the third month,
Minister of Education (Sīkōng) Lú Yù passed away.
In the summer, fourth month, on the guǐmǎo day,
an edict said:
“Officials and people of Gāoxiǎn county, Xuántú Commandery, rebelled,
and the chief, Zhèng Xī, was killed by the rebels.
The commoner Wáng Jiǎn carried Xī’s coffin,
traveling day and night like a star,
bringing it far to his home province;
his loyalty and integrity are admirable.
Therefore, Jiǎn is specially appointed as Commandant of Loyalty and Righteousness (Zhōngyì Dūwèi),
to commend his extraordinary conduct.”
On the jiǎzǐ day,
General Who Attacks the East (Zhēngdōng Dàjiāngjūn) Zhūgě Dàn was made Minister of Education (Sīkōng).
In the fifth month, on the xīnwèi day,
the Emperor visited Bìyōng,
and commanded his officials to compose poems.
Attendant Councilor (Shìzhōng) Hé Yōu, Director of the Department of State Affairs (Shàngshū) Chén Qiān, and others were slow in writing their poems,
and the authorities proposed their removal from office.
An edict said:
“Being ignorant,
We delight in refined literature
and widely invite poems and essays
to understand gains and losses.
That it should cause such contention
truly makes Us uneasy.
Therefore, pardon Yōu and others.
Let the responsible officials instruct that from now on,
all officials must study ancient principles
and cultivate and clarify the classics,
to accord with Our intention.”
On the yǐhài day,
Zhūgě Dàn did not accept the summons,
raised troops in rebellion,
and killed the Inspector of Yángzhōu, Yuè Lín.
On the bǐngzǐ day,
an amnesty was granted to the officers, soldiers, and people of Huáinán who had been misled by Dàn.
On the dīngchǒu day,
an edict said:
“Zhūgě Dàn created a violent rebellion,
overturning Yángzhōu.
In the past, when Qíng Bù rebelled,
Emperor Gāozǔ of Hàn personally led the army;
when Kuí Xiāo defied,
Emperor Guāngwǔ marched west;
and when Emperor Lièzǔ Míng personally campaigned against Wú and Shǔ,
all were to display their awe-inspiring might
and glorify their military prowess.
Now, the Empress Dowager and We should temporarily lead the army together
to quickly subdue the vile enemy
and bring peace to the eastern region.”
On the jǐmǎo day,
an edict said:
“Zhūgě Dàn instigated rebellion,
coercing the loyal and righteous.
General Who Pacifies Bandits (Píngkòu Jiāngjūn), Marquis of Línwèi Pavilion (Línwèi Tínghóu) Páng Huì, and Cavalry Commander (Jìdū) Adjutant General (Piānjiāngjūn) Lù Fān,
each with their subordinates,
broke through the gates and charged out.
Their loyalty, bravery, and fierce courage
are worthy of commendation and distinction.
Therefore, promote Huì’s peerage to Marquis of a District (Xiānghóu),
and enfeoff Fān as Marquis of a Pavilion (Tínghóu).”
In the sixth month, on the yǐsì day,
an edict said:
“Sūn Yī,

the Wú envoy, Bearer of the Imperial Seal (Chíjié), Supervisor of All Military Affairs in Xiàkǒu (Dūdū Xiàkǒu Zhūjūnshì), General Who Guards the Army (Zhènjūn Jiāngjūn), and Marquis of Shāxiàn (Shāxiàn Hóu),
a branch of the rebels,
holding the position of a senior general,
fearing Heaven and knowing fate,
deeply discerning fortune and misfortune,
suddenly led his multitude
to return afar to our great nation.
Even Wēizǐ leaving Yīn,
or Yuè Yì fleeing Yān,
could not surpass this.

Therefore, appoint Yī as Attendant Councilor (Shìzhōng), General of Chariots and Cavalry (Chējì Jiāngjūn), Bearer of the Imperial Seal (Jiǎjié), Governor of Jiāozhōu (Jiāozhōu Mù), and Marquis of Wú (Wú Hóu),
open a mansion (kāifǔ) to summon and appoint officials, with status equal to the Three Excellencies (Yítóng Sānsī),
following the ancient rites of a marquis or count of eight honors,
wearing a yǎn crown and red shoes;
treat him with great generosity.”
On the jiǎzǐ day,
an edict said:
“Now the imperial carriage is stationed at Xiàng,
and the Great General is reverently executing the celestial punishment,
advancing to the Huái Pǔ.
In the past, when the Chancellor of State (Xiàngguó) and Grand Commandant (Dà Sīmǎ) led campaigns,
they always went with the Department of State Affairs (Shàngshū).
Now it should be as of old.”
Thereupon, Grand Master of Remonstrance (Sànqí Chángshì) Péi Xiù and Palace Attendant (Gěishì Huángmén Shìláng) Zhōng Huì were both ordered to go with the Great General.
In the autumn, eighth month,
an edict said:
“In the past, when the Prince of Yān Cì conspired to rebel,
Hán Yì and others remonstrated and died,
and the Hàn court prominently elevated their sons.
When Zhūgě Dàn created a violent rebellion,
Chief Clerk (Zhǔbù) Xuān Lóng and Company Commander (Bùqúdū) Qín Jié upheld their integrity and righteousness,
and firmly contended against him in the face of danger,
for which they were killed by Dàn.
This is what is meant by ‘not having the kinship of Bǐ Gàn yet suffering his fate.’
Therefore, make the sons of Lóng and Jié Cavalry Commandants (Jì Dūwèi),
and add gifts and rewards,
to brilliantly display to near and far
their exceptional loyalty and righteousness.”
In the ninth month,
a general amnesty was issued.
In the winter, twelfth month,
Wú great generals Quán Duān, Quán Yì, and others led their multitudes to surrender.
In the third year, spring, second month,
Great General Sīmǎ Wén Wáng captured Shòuchūn city
and beheaded Zhūgě Dàn.
In the third month,
an edict said:
“In ancient times, when an enemy was defeated,
their bodies were collected to form a Jingguan (京觀, capital-view mound),
to deter perversity and rebellion and manifest military achievements.
During the Yuándǐng reign of Emperor Xiàowǔ of Hàn,
Tóngxiāng was renamed Wénxǐ,
and Xīnxiāng was renamed Huòjiā,
to mark the downfall of Nányuè.
The Great General personally commanded the six armies,
established his camp at Qiūtóu,
pacified the internal great villains,
and annihilated the external bandits and enemies.
His achievements saved the myriad people,
and his renown shook the four seas.
The place where the enemy was defeated
should bear an auspicious name.
Therefore, change Qiūtóu to Wǔqiū,
to clearly indicate that the rebellion was pacified by military might,
and that future generations will not forget.
This also carries the meaning of the Jingguan of the two districts.”
In the summer, fifth month,
Great General Sīmǎ Wén Wáng was ordered to be Chancellor of State (Xiàngguó),
enfeoffed as Duke of Jìn (Jìn Gōng),
with an eating-tax of eight commanderies,
and additionally granted the Nine Bestowals (Jiǔ Xī).
Wén Wáng declined nine times before it was dropped.
In the sixth month, on the bǐngzǐ day,
an edict said:
“In the past, mountain bandits in Nányáng Commandery caused disturbance,
intending to kidnap and hold hostage the former Administrator (Tàishǒu) Dōnglǐ Gǔn.
Assistant of Merit (Gōngcáo) Yìng Yú single-handedly defended Gǔn,
and thus he escaped the danger.
Yú fell and perished,
sacrificing his life to save his lord.
Let the Minister of Works (Sītú) appoint Yú’s grandson Lún as an official,
so that he may receive the reward for his ancestor’s unwavering loyalty.”
On the xīn-mǎo day,
a great deliberation was held concerning the merits of the Huáinán campaign.
Titles and rewards were granted, each according to their distinctions.
In autumn, in the eighth month, on the jiǎ-xū day,
Píqi Jiāngjūn Wáng Chǎng was appointed Sīkōng.
On the bǐng-yín day,
an imperial edict stated:
"To nurture the elderly and promote education
is how the Three Dynasties established customs and left an imperishable legacy.
There must be Sānlǎo and Wǔgēng to highly honor respect,
solicit opinions, and accept advice,
as recorded in the Dūnshǐ.
Only then will the whole world follow the flow
and be transformed by observing.
It is fitting to carefully select individuals of virtue and conduct
to fill these positions.
Guānnèi Hóu Wáng Xiáng
embodies benevolence and upholds righteousness;
his ambition is refined and solid.
Guānnèi Hóu Zhèng Xiǎotóng
is gentle, respectful, filial, and friendly,
adhering to ritual without error.
Therefore, appoint Wáng Xiáng as Sānlǎo
and Zhèng Xiǎotóng as Wǔgēng."
The imperial carriage personally led the various officials,
performing the ancient rites.
In this year,
a blue dragon (Qīnglóng) and a yellow dragon (Huánglóng) were seen consecutively in wells in the counties of Dùnqīu, Guānjùn, and Yángxià.
In the fourth year, in spring, in the first month,
two yellow dragons
were seen in a well in Nínglíng County.
In summer, in the sixth month,
Sīkōng Wáng Chǎng passed away.
In autumn, in the seventh month,
Chénliú Wáng Jùn passed away.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the bǐng-yín day,
Xīnchéng Commandery was divided,
and Shàngyōng Commandery was re-established.
In the eleventh month, on the guǐ-mǎo day,
Chējì Jiāngjūn Sūn Yī was murdered by a maid.
In the fifth year, in spring, on the first day of the first month,
there was a solar eclipse.
In summer, in the fourth month,
an imperial edict commanded the relevant officials to follow the previous order
and promote Dàjiāngjūn Sīmǎ Wénwáng to the position of Xiàngguó,
enfeoff him as Jìn Gōng,
and bestow upon him the Jiǔxī.
In the fifth month, on the jǐ-chǒu day,
Gāoguì Xiānggōng passed away,
aged twenty.
The Huáng Tàihòu issued an order saying:
"I, in my unworthiness,
encountered a misfortune in my family.
Formerly, I supported and established Dōnghǎi Wáng Zǐmáo
as the heir of Míngdì,
seeing his fondness for books, memorials, and literature,
hoping he could achieve success.
But his temperament was violent and unruly,
growing worse by the day.
I repeatedly rebuked him,
but he became even more indignant and enraged,
fabricating ugly, rebellious, and impious words to slander me,
thus severing relations between the two palaces.
What he said
was intolerable to hear,
something that heaven and earth could not cover or support.
I secretly ordered Dàjiāngjūn,
saying that he could not serve the ancestral temple,
fearing that the state would be overthrown,
and I would have no face to see the late emperor after death.
Dàjiāngjūn, considering him still young,
believed he would change his heart for the better,
and earnestly maintained his position.
But this child was furious and violent,
his actions becoming increasingly egregious.
He raised a crossbow and shot into my palace from afar,
cursing that it should hit my neck,
and the arrow fell right in front of me.
I told Dàjiāngjūn that he must be deposed,
dozens of times, repeatedly.
This child heard all of it,
knew his guilt was heavy,
and then plotted assassination,
bribing my attendants,
so that when I took medicine,
they would secretly poison it,
a double scheme.
The matter was exposed.
He intended to seize the opportunity to lead troops into the Western Palace to kill me,
then go out to seize Dàjiāngjūn,
and summon Shìzhōng Wáng Shěn, Sànqí Chángshì Wáng Yè,
and Shàngshū Wáng Jīng.
He took out a yellow silk edict from his bosom and showed it to them,
saying that it was to be implemented today.
My danger
was greater than piled eggs.
I am old and widowed,
how could I cherish my remaining life so much?
But I am grieved that the late emperor's wishes were not fulfilled,
and that the state would be overthrown, that is the pain.
Thanks to the spirits of the ancestral temple,
Wáng Shěn and Wáng Yè immediately rushed to inform Dàjiāngjūn,
who was able to prepare strict warnings in advance.
And this child then led his attendants out of the Yúnlóng Gate,
beat the battle drums,
personally drew his blade,
and with his attendants and guards, entered between the military formations,
and was killed by the vanguard.
This child not only acted rebelliously and impiously,
but also brought great disaster upon himself,
causing me unspeakable sorrow.
Formerly, Hàn Chāngyì Wáng was deposed as a commoner due to his crimes.
This child should also be buried with the rites of a commoner,
so that all within and without know of this child's actions.
Furthermore, Shàngshū Wáng Jīng
was vicious and utterly lawless;
arrest Wáng Jīng and his family members and send them all to the Tíngwèi."
On the gēng-yín day,
Tàifù Fú, Dàjiāngjūn Wén Wáng, Tàiwèi Ròu, and Sītú Chōng bowed their heads and said:
"We humbly observe the middle order,
that the former Gāoguì Xiānggōng acted rebelliously and impiously,
bringing great disaster upon himself.
Following the precedent of Hàn Chāngyì Wáng's deposition for crimes,
he is to be buried with the rites of a commoner.
We, your ministers, holding our positions,
were unable to rectify the chaos
and restrain the wicked rebels.
Upon receiving the order, we are shaken with fear,
our hearts trembling with sorrow.
According to the principle of the Chūnqiū,
a king has no outside (i.e., no superior),
yet it records 'Xiāng Wáng went out to reside in Zhèng,'
because he could not serve his mother,
and was therefore cut off from his position.
Now Gāoguì Xiānggōng brazenly acted unlawfully,
almost endangering the state,
and brought ruin upon himself.
He is abandoned by both gods and men.
To bury him with the rites of a commoner
is truly in accordance with ancient precedents.
However, we your ministers humbly believe that Your Highness's benevolence and compassion are exceedingly profound.
Although upholding great righteousness,
you still show sorrow and pity.
Our hearts truly cannot bear it,
and we believe that grace should be extended,
and he should be buried with the rites of a king."
The Tàihòu agreed.
She sent an envoy, holding a jié, the acting Zhōng Hùjūn and Zhōnglěi Jiāngjūn Sīmǎ Yán, to the north to welcome Chángdào Xiānggōng Huáng to succeed Míngdì.
On the mǎo day,
the various dukes memorialized the Tàihòu, saying:
"Your Highness's sagely virtue shines brightly,
bringing peace and order to the whole world,
yet you still refer to your commands as 'order' (lìng),
which is the same as for a vassal state.
We request that from now on, Your Highness's official documents
all be referred to as 'imperial edict' (zhào zhì),
as per the precedents of former generations."
On the guǐ-mǎo day,
Dàjiāngjūn firmly declined the honors of Xiàngguó, Jìn Gōng, and the Jiǔxī.
The Tàihòu issued an edict saying:
"To not conceal one's achievements
is a great principle of the Zhōu Yì.
To help others achieve their good
is cherished by ancient sages.
Now, I heed your insistence,
allowing your expression to be shown outwardly,
to manifest the duke's humble light."
On the day *wùshēn*,
Grand General Wénwáng reported:
"The Gāoguì Xiānggōng led the imperial guards and soldiers,
drew their blades and sounded gongs and drums towards my residence.
Fearing a clash of weapons,
I immediately ordered my generals and soldiers not to cause any harm,
and that those who violated the order would be dealt with by military law.
The Cavalry Supervisor Chéng Cuì's younger brother, Crown Prince's Household Administrator Jì,
suddenly entered the ranks and wounded the Duke,
which led to his demise.
I immediately apprehended Jì and applied military law.
I have heard that the principle for a subject
is to die without a second thought,
and the duty of serving the ruler
is not to shrink from hardship.
Previously, when the sudden calamity occurred,
and disaster struck like a triggered mechanism,
I truly wished to devote myself to death,
abiding by whatever fate decreed.
However, considering that the original plot was to endanger the Empress Dowager,
and overthrow the ancestral temple,
I, who unworthily hold a great responsibility,
have the duty to stabilize the nation.
I feared that even if I died,
my blame would be even heavier.
Wishing to follow the precedents of Yī and Zhōu in exercising authority,
to stabilize the nation in this crisis,
I immediately issued successive orders
not to approach the imperial carriage.
However, Jì rushed into the ranks,
leading to this great change.
My sorrow and bitter regret
rend my innermost being.
I know not where I can fall to my death.
The law stipulates that for great treason and lawlessness,
parents, wife, children, and siblings are all to be executed.
Jì was violent, rebellious, and defiant,
interfering with the state and disrupting order;
his crime is beyond pardon.
I immediately ordered the Imperial Censor to arrest Jì's family
and hand them over to the Grand Judge,
to determine their guilt."
The Empress Dowager issued an edict saying:
"Among the crimes punishable by the five punishments,
none is greater than unfilial conduct.
If a person has an unfilial child,
they still report it for judgment.
How can this boy ever again be a ruler?
We, a woman, do not comprehend great righteousness,
and believe that Jì should not be immediately considered guilty of great treason.
However, the Grand General's determination and sincerity are earnest,
and his words are mournful;
therefore, we grant what has been petitioned.
It should be announced throughout the empire,
so that all may know the full story."
In the sixth month, on the day *guǐchǒu*,
an edict stated:
"In ancient times, when a ruler chose a personal name or courtesy name,
it was difficult to offend but easy to avoid.
Now, the Chángdào Xiānggōng's personal name and courtesy name are very difficult to avoid.
Let the court officials broadly deliberate and propose changes,
submitting their recommendations."
Chénliú Wáng's personal name was Huàn,
and his courtesy name was Jǐngmíng.
He was a grandson of Wǔdì,
and the son of Yān Wáng Yǔ.
In the third year of Gānlù,
he was enfeoffed as Chángdào Xiānggōng of Āncì County.
When Gāoguì Xiānggōng died,
the high officials discussed and welcomed him to the throne.
In the sixth month, on the day *jiǎyín*,
he entered Luòyáng,
and met the Empress Dowager.
On that day, he ascended the imperial throne at the Tàijí Qiándiàn,
issued a great amnesty,
changed the era name,
and bestowed official ranks, grain, and silk upon the common people, each with different grades.
In the sixth month of summer, on the day *bǐngchén* of the first year of Jǐngyuán,
Grand General Sīmǎ Wénwáng's position was advanced to Xiàngguó,
and he was enfeoffed as Jìn Gōng,
with an increase of two commanderies in his enfeoffment,
making a total of ten with previous grants.
He was granted the Nine Bestowals,
all as previously [decreed].
All his kinsmen and younger relatives who were not yet marquises were enfeoffed as Tínghóu,
and granted ten million cash
and ten thousand bolts of silk.
Wénwáng firmly declined, and it was stopped.
On the day *jǐwèi*,
the former Emperor Xiàndì of Hàn's consort Jié passed away.
The Emperor personally mourned at Huálínyuán,
and sent an envoy with a staff of authority to posthumously honor the consort as Xiànmù Huánghòu.
For the burial,
the chariots, clothing, and regulations all followed the precedents of the Hàn dynasty.
On the day *guǐhài*,
Wáng Guān, Minister of the Right of the Department of State Affairs, was appointed Sīkōng.
In the tenth month of winter,
Guān passed away.
In the eleventh month,
Yān Wáng submitted a memorial congratulating the emperor on the winter solstice,
referring to himself as a subject.
An edict stated:
"In ancient times, some rulers
did not treat all as their subjects.
Yān Wáng should follow this principle.
Why does the memorial not refer to him as a subject?
Also, there should be a reply.
He who succeeds to the great lineage
should lower his private relations.
How much more so when the succession is so significant!
To treat him simply as a subject or concubine
is also not what the heart feels at ease with.
Let everything be handled according to the rites and classics,
ensuring that it is done appropriately."
The officials concerned reported,
believing that
"there is no greater禮 (ritual) than honoring ancestors,
and no greater system than rectifying the classics.
Your Majesty, by virtue of your accumulated virtue and the predestined timing,
rules over all nations,
succeeds to the weight of the great lineage,
and extends the foundation of the three ancestors.
We humbly believe that Yān Wáng, by virtue of his noble kinship,
holds his rightful position as a feudal lord,
personally upholds reverence and solemnity,
and leads all nations in respectful virtue.
As for the established classics,
which proclaim great harmony and are not to be controlled,
the sacred court should indeed honor him with extraordinary regulations,
and serve him with the礼 (rite) of not treating him as a subject.
We, your subjects, unanimously agree that Yān Wáng's memorials
may be allowed to follow the old format.
As for the imperial edict's promulgation,
it may be that a good question is implied.
According to the principles of righteousness,
it is like 'the reverence of a Yan audience.'
It is appropriate to slightly conform to the sacred reverence,
increase the ceremonial title,
and show that one dares not address him directly.
It should be: 'The Emperor respectfully inquires of the Great King's attendants.'
As for imperial rescripts,
they are the formal statutes of the state,
by which the court distinguishes public regulations
and proclaims norms and standards to the world.
They should follow the law;
therefore, it is 'Rescript to Yān Wáng.'
In all imperial orders,
rescripts,
reports to the throne,
and memorials, wherever Yān Wáng is mentioned,
the character '王' (Wáng) should be pronounced in the rising tone.
Except for matters related to ancestral temple sacrifices,
his royal name should not be used.
In reports to the throne, memorials, documents, and by officials and common people, his royal taboo name should not be violated,
to illustrate the special rites
accorded to him, surpassing other lords.
This upholds the royal standard of honoring ancestors above,
and complies with the earnest feelings of sacred reverence below.
If these two are not amiss,
the rites will truly be appropriate.
This should be universally announced and implemented."
In the twelfth month, on the day *jiǎshēn*,
a yellow dragon was seen in a well in Huáyīn County.
On the day *jiǎwǔ*,
Wáng Xiáng, Intendant of the Capital, was appointed Sīkōng.
In the fifth month of summer of the second year, on the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
In the seventh month of autumn,
the foreign peoples of Hán and Wèimò from Lèlàng came with their tribes to pay tribute.
In the eighth month, on the day *wùyín*,
Zhào Wáng Gàn passed away.
On the day *jiǎyín*,
the Grand General was again commanded to be advanced to the rank of Jìn Gōng,
and his position was added as Xiàngguó,
with complete rites and generous bestowals,
all as previously decreed;
he again firmly declined, and it was stopped.
In the second month of spring of the third year,
a green dragon was seen in a well in Zhǐ County.
In the fourth month of summer,
the commandery of Liáodōng reported that the state of Sùshèn had sent envoys who, through multiple interpreters, came to pay tribute,
presenting thirty bows from their country,
three feet five inches long,
and arrows made of *hú* wood, one foot eight inches long,
three hundred stone crossbow bolts,
and twenty suits of armor made of leather, bone, and iron.
And four hundred sable furs.
In the tenth month of winter,
Jiāng Wéi, Grand General of Shǔ, invaded Táoyáng.
Zhèn Xī Jiāngjūn Dèng Ài resisted him,
and defeated Wéi at Hòuhé.
Wéi fled.
In this year,
an edict ordered the sacrifice to the former military libationer Guō Jiā in the Tàizǔ ancestral temple court.
In the second month of spring of the fourth year,
the Grand General was again commanded to be advanced in rank and granted bestowals, all as previously decreed;
he again firmly declined, and it was stopped.
In the fifth month of summer,
an imperial edict stated:
"Shǔ,
a paltry small state,
with limited territory and sparse population,
yet Jiāng Wéi cruelly used its populace,
never giving up his ambition.
After the devastating defeat of previous years,
he still resumed farming in Tàzhōng,
harshly exploiting the various Qiāng tribes,
with endless labor,
the people could not endure their plight.
To conquer the weak and attack the ignorant
is the excellent principle of military strategy;
to compel others without being compelled by them
is the supreme stratagem of a military strategist.
The only one Shǔ relies on
is Wéi.
Since he is far from his lair,
it will be easy to exert force.
Now, let General Who Conquers the West, Dèng Ài, command all the armies
to proceed to Gānsōng and Tàzhōng to capture Wéi.
Let the Inspector of Yōngzhōu, Zhūgě Xù, command the armies to proceed to Wǔdū and Gāolóu,
to attack him from front and rear.
If Wéi is captured,
we shall then advance simultaneously from east and west,
and sweep away Bāshǔ."
He further ordered General Who Guards the West, Zhōng Huì, to attack Shǔ via Luògǔ.
In the ninth month of autumn,
Grand Commandant Gāo Róu passed away.
On the jiǎyín day of the tenth month of winter,
an edict again commanded that the Grand General be promoted in rank and awarded titles and gifts as per the previous decree.
On the guǐmǎo day,
Empress Biàn was established.
In the eleventh month,
a general amnesty was proclaimed.
Since Dèng Ài and Zhōng Huì led their troops to attack Shǔ,
they conquered every place they reached.
In this month,
the Lord of Shǔ, Liú Chán, went to Dèng Ài and surrendered,
and Bāshǔ was completely pacified.
On the gēngxū day of the twelfth month,
Minister of Works Zhèng Chōng was made Grand Guardian.
On the rénzǐ day,
Yìzhōu was divided into Liángzhōu.
On the guǐchǒu day,
a special amnesty was granted to the officials and people of Yìzhōu,
and half of their rent and taxes were remitted for five years.
On the yǐmǎo day,
General Who Conquers the West, Dèng Ài, was made Grand Commandant,
and General Who Guards the West, Zhōng Huì, was made Minister of Works.
The Empress Dowager passed away.
In the first month of spring of Xiánxī First Year, on the rénxū day,
Dèng Ài was summoned in a caged cart.
On the jiǎzǐ day,
the Emperor traveled to Cháng'ān.
On the rénshēn day,
an envoy was sent to offer jade and silk to Mount Huà.
In this month,
Zhōng Huì rebelled in Shǔ
and was suppressed by the populace;
Dèng Ài was also killed.
On the xīnmǎo day of the second month,
a special amnesty was granted to all those in the territory of Yìzhōu.
On the gēngshēn day,
Empress Míngyuán Guō was buried.
On the dīngchǒu day of the third month,
Minister of Works Wáng Xiáng was made Grand Commandant,
General Who Conquers the North Hé Zēng was made Minister of Works,
and Left Assistant of the Department of State Affairs Xún Yǐ was made Minister of Works.
On the jǐmǎo day,
the Duke of Jìn was promoted to King,
enfeoffed with ten commanderies,
making a total of twenty including the previous ones.
On the dīnghài day,
Liú Chán was enfeoffed as Duke of Ānlè.
On the gēngshēn day of the fifth month of summer,
the Prime Minister and King of Jìn memorialized to restore the five ranks of nobility.
On the jiǎxū day,
the era name was changed.
On the guǐwèi day,
a posthumous order designated Marquis Xuānwén of Wǔyáng as King Xuān of Jìn,
and Marquis Zhōngwǔ of Wǔyáng as King Jǐng of Jìn.
In the sixth month,
General Who Guards the West, Wèi Guàn, reported that the Yōngzhōu army had seized a jade seal in Chéngdū county,
and the inscription on the seal resembled the characters
"Chéng Xìn".
Following the meaning of King Chéng of Zhōu returning the harvested grain,
it was proclaimed to all officials
and stored in the Prime Minister's residence.
Originally,
since the pacification of Shǔ,
the Wú invaders had been besieging Yǒng'ān,
and the armies of Jīng and Yù were dispatched to assist.
In the seventh month,
the bandits all retreated.
On the gēngyín day of the eighth month,
the Emperor ordered the Central Army Protector Sīmǎ Yán to assist in the Prime Minister's affairs,
in the same manner as Duke of Lǔ was honored in the past.
On the guǐsì day,
an imperial edict stated:
"Previously, the treacherous minister Zhōng Huì instigated a rebellion,
gathered the campaigning generals and soldiers,
coerced them with military might,
first revealed his wicked plot,
spoke rebellious words,
intimidated the multitude,
and made them all discuss it.
In that urgent moment,
none were not startled and fearful.
The Prime Minister's Left Aide, Xiàhóu Hé, and the Knight-Cavalry Subordinate, Zhū Fǔ, were in Chéngdū at the time;
Central Army Commander Sīmǎ Jiǎ Fǔ and Palace Attendant Yáng Xiù each participated in Zhōng Huì's military affairs.
Hé, Xiù, and Fǔ all maintained their integrity and did not yield,
resisted Zhōng Huì's wicked words,
faced danger without hesitation,
and their words were righteous and ardent.
Fǔ spoke to the disbanded general Wáng Qǐ,
saying, 'Zhōng Huì is treacherous, rebellious, and violent,
and wishes to kill all the generals and soldiers,'
and also said, 'The Prime Minister has already led 300,000 troops west to attack Zhōng Huì,'
intending to exaggerate the situation
and stir up the hearts of the multitude.
Wáng Qǐ went out
and proclaimed Fǔ's words to all the armies,
thus making the generals and soldiers even more inspired and determined.
It is fitting to bestow great honors
to display their loyalty and righteousness.
Therefore, promote Hé and Fǔ to Marquis of a District,
and Xiù and Fǔ to Marquis Within the Pass.
Wáng Qǐ, who publicized Fǔ's words
and informed the generals and soldiers,
should also be specially rewarded.
Therefore, make Wáng Qǐ a Commander of a Unit."
On the guǐmǎo day,
General Who Guards the Army, Sīmǎ Wàng, was made General of Agile Cavalry.
On the wǔwǔ day of the ninth month,
Central Army Protector Sīmǎ Yán was made Grand General of the Protecting Army.
On the xīnwèi day,
an imperial edict stated:
"The Wú bandits' government and punishments are tyrannical,
and their levies are endless.
Sūn Xiū sent an envoy, Dèng Jù,
to order the Administrator of Jiāozhǐ to arrest and send its people,
to be conscripted as soldiers.
The Wú general Lǚ Xīng, taking advantage of the people's anger,
and hearing that our royal army had pacified Bāshǔ,
immediately gathered local heroes,
executed Dèng Jù and others,
expelled the Administrators and Chief Officials,
pacified the officials and people,
to await the imperial command.
The commanderies of Jiǔzhēn and Rìnán, hearing that Xīng had abandoned rebellion and submitted,
also unanimously responded,
and cooperated with Xīng.
Xīng sent letters to the prefectures and commanderies of Rìnán,
explaining the grand strategy,
marching his army to Hépǔ,
informing them of fortune and misfortune.
He sent Commandant Táng Pǔ and others to Jìnchéng county,
and through the Southern Central Military Governor and Protector of the Army Huò Yì, submitted a memorial to declare his intentions.
Furthermore, the generals and officials of Jiāozhǐ each submitted memorials,
saying, 'Xīng initiated this undertaking,
and all, great and small, obeyed his command.
The commandery has mountain bandits,
who are connected with various other commanderies,
and we fear their differing intentions,
and that they may harbor disloyalty.
As a temporary measure, it is appropriate to appoint Xīng as Supervisor of All Military Affairs in Jiāozhōu, Supreme General, and Marquis of Dìng'ān County,
and we beg for imperial commendation and reward,
to comfort this remote borderland.'
Their sincere intentions
were expressed in their words.
In the past, Yí Fù paid homage to Lǔ,
which the Spring and Autumn Annals praised;
Dòu Róng submitted to Hàn,
and was treated with special courtesy.
Now, the imperial might shakes afar,
embracing and pacifying the six directions,
encompassing all remote tribes,
and unifying the four quarters.
Xīng was the first to turn towards our transforming influence,
and led his multitude to submit,
racing thousands of miles with righteousness,
requesting officials to assume their duties.
It is appropriate to bestow favor upon him,
and elevate his rank.
This will make Xīng and others cherish loyalty and feel joyful,
and when distant people hear of it,
they will surely all eagerly strive to follow.
Therefore, make Xīng Inspector-General, Supervisor of All Military Affairs in Jiāozhōu, Grand General of the Southern Central Region,
and Marquis of Dìng'ān County,
granting him the authority to act as he deems fit,
reporting later what he has done."
Before the imperial edict arrived,
Xīng was killed by his subordinates.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the *dìnghài* day,
an imperial edict stated:
“In ancient times, sagely emperors and enlightened kings,
calming chaos and saving the world,
preserving the great and establishing achievements,
though their civil and martial paths differed,
their meritorious achievements were united.
Thus, some brandished shields and axes to instruct the unruly,
while others arrayed their armies to awe the violent and arrogant.
As for loving the people and preserving the state,
and bestowing prosperity upon all creatures,
they invariably first cultivated civil education,
and demonstrated proper conduct.
Only when there was no other recourse did they resort to military force;
this is what great virtues have in common.
Previously, during the collapse of the Jì-Hàn,
the entire land was overturned,
and Liú Bèi and Sūn Quán seized the opportunity to create strife.
The Three Ancestors pacified and tranquilized the central plains,
working ceaselessly,
thus allowing the remaining bandits to usurp and rebel for generations.
Fortunately, relying on the awesome spiritual power of the ancestral temples,
and the loyal and martial宰辅 [zǎifǔ] (grand counselors),
troops were mobilized from all four directions,
to expand and secure Yōng and Shǔ.
The campaign did not last a full season,
and was won in a single expedition.
Recently, the region south of the Jiāng has fallen into decay,
its governance and laws have become dark and chaotic.
With Bā and Hàn pacified,
they are isolated, weak, and without aid.
Jiāo, Jīng, Yáng, and Yuè
have all turned towards us like grass in the wind.
Now, the伪将 [wěijiàng] (false general) Lǚ Xīng of Jiāozhǐ has already led three commanderies,
and pledged allegiance from a thousand *lǐ* away;
Yán Děng, the邑侯 [yìhóu] (marquis of the town) of Wǔlíng and minister, has gathered five counties,
and requested to become our subjects;
mountain people from Lúlíng, Yùzhāng, have rebelled against Wú en masse,
using the name of supporting the Northern General.
Moreover, Sūn Xiū has died of illness,
the chief commander has been replaced,
the country is in disarray,
and each person has their own intentions.
The false general Shī Jì,
a renowned official of the rebels,
is filled with doubt and suspicion,
and is deeply feared and hated.
With his followers rebelling and his kin departing,
none have firm resolve.
From ancient times to the present,
there has never been such a clear sign of impending doom.
If the six armies were to display their might,
and approach the Jiāng and Hàn from the south,
the region of Wú-Kuài would certainly lead the old and carry the young to welcome the royal army;
this is an inevitable principle.
However, mobilizing large armies
still entails labor and expense.
It is appropriate to inform them of our awe-inspiring virtue,
and reveal our benevolence and trustworthiness,
so they may understand the benefits of submission and harmony.
Xú Shào, Aide to the Grand Counselor, and Sūn Yù, Officer of the Water Bureau,
were captured
together at Shòuchūn.
Shào was originally the false Superintendent of Nánlíng,
possessing talent and vigor;
Yù
was a collateral relative of Sūn Quán,
loyal and clear-sighted in affairs.
Let Shào be sent back south,
with Yù as his deputy,
to proclaim the national mandate,
and address the Wú people.
All that is conveyed
shall be based on facts.
If they awaken to this,
it will not harm our plans for conquest.
This is a long-standing strategy of achieving victory in the ancestral temple,
a way from ancient times.
Let Shào concurrently hold the position of Mounted Regular Attendant,
be granted the rank of Commandant of the Chariot Guards,
and enfeoffed as Marquis of the Capital Pavilion;
Yù shall concurrently serve as Attendant at the Yellow Gate,
and be granted the title of Marquis within the Pass.
The concubines and male and female family members of Shào and others who are currently here
are all permitted to accompany them,
to demonstrate the benevolence of the state,
and they need not be returned,
to widely broadcast great trust.”
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Commandant of the Pacifying Army, Grand General, Marquis of Xīnchāng Township, Yán, was appointed Heir Apparent of Jìn.
In this year,
the *túntián* officials were abolished to equalize political labor.
All *diǎnnóng* became Grand Administrators,
and all Commandants became Magistrates or Chiefs;
Shǔ people who were willing to relocate internally were encouraged and recruited,
and given provisions for two years,
and exempted from corvée for twenty years.
The counties of Ānmí and Fúlù each reported the growth of auspicious grain.
In the second year, in spring, in the second month, on the *jiǎchén* day,
Qú county captured an auspicious turtle and presented it,
which was then returned to the Grand Counselor’s Residence.
On the *gēngxū* day,
because Zhāng Xiū, a Tiger Swift, had ridden swiftly to various camps in Chéngdū to report Zhōng Huì’s rebellion,
even to the point of sacrificing his life,
Xiū’s younger brother, Yǐ, was granted the title of Marquis within the Pass.
In summer, in the fourth month,
